# DogsBay XML

> The XML and DITA editor with an AI agent that understands your content model.

## Documentation

- [Home](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs.md): An XML and DITA editor with an AI agent that works on your content model and shows you every change before it lands.

## Getting started

- [What DogsBay XML is](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/getting-started/what-it-is.md): What the editor does, who it is for, and the three ideas that shape it.
- [Installing](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/getting-started/install.md): Install DogsBay XML, put its command line on your PATH, and turn on the integration server.
- [Tutorial: fixing a DITA guide](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/getting-started/tutorial.md): Open a real DITA project that has problems in it, find them with the project tools, and fix some of them with the AI agent.

## Working with the agent

- [The agent, and what it may touch](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/agent/overview.md): How the built-in agent and hosted agents differ, which tools they get, and the limits that apply before any change reaches a file.
- [Reviewing an agent's changes](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/agent/proposals.md): Agent edits to DITA files arrive as tracked changes. Accept them, reject them, or comment on them.
- [Using Claude Code, Codex or Gemini](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/agent/hosted-agents.md): Run an agent you already have inside the editor, and lend it the editor's DITA tools.

## Authoring DITA

- [Topics and maps](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/authoring/topics-and-maps.md): Write topics in the source or Author view, assemble them into maps, and edit map structure without breaking references.
- [Keys and reuse](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/authoring/keys-and-reuse.md): Resolve keys across a map, convert direct references to keys, and move shared content into reuse topics.
- [Conditional content](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/authoring/conditional-content.md): Profile content with conditions, filter it with DITAVAL, and keep the values under control with a subject scheme.
- [Metadata](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/authoring/metadata.md): Define which metadata topics must carry, audit the project against it, and fill in what is missing.

## Finding and changing

- [Validating a project](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/finding/validation.md): Check one document or a whole set against its grammar, business rules and references, and use the same checks as a build gate.
- [Refactoring](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/finding/refactoring.md): Rename, move, split and restructure content without breaking the references that point at it.

## Publishing

- [Previewing and publishing](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/publishing/publishing.md): See a styled preview while you write, then build deliverables with DITA-OT.

## Automation

- [Connecting an AI assistant](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/automation/mcp.md): Expose the editor's DITA operations to Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Cursor over MCP.

## Reference

- [Menu reference](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/reference/menus.md): Every menu in the editor, in order, with what each command does and where it is documented in full.
- [Panel reference](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/reference/panels.md): Every panel in the sidebars and the bottom bar, what it shows, and what you can do in it.
- [The command line](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/reference/cli.md): What dogsbay-xml can do, grouped by what you are trying to find out or change.

## For developers

- [Building from source](https://dogsbay.ai/dogsbay-xml-docs/developers/build-from-source.md): Build the editor with Gradle, and run the command line from a checkout or from the uber-jar on a machine with no installer.
